01.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
01.event: They intend to rule per a baraita permitting a nursing mother to remarry; an old woman tells them Rav Nahman forbade it to her
01.turn: Rav Pappi reminds them of the baraita of Rabbi Meir and Shmuel's ruling
01.outcome: They admit they had forgotten; the Gemara states the halakha and alludes to a woman who strangled her child
01.summary: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to permit a nursing mother to remarry when an old woman told them Rav Nahman had forbidden it in her own case. Rav Pappi cited a baraita and Shmuel's ruling against them, and they conceded they had forgotten it. The rest is legal discussion and an incident only alluded to.
01.missing: No narrated action actually taken; the old woman's case and the strangling are only alluded to.
01.reason: Mainly speech and legal discussion with an intended ruling that is averted and incidents only alluded to; some event and change, so borderline rather than not.

02.actor: A depositor and the family of Rabbi Meyasha
02.event: A man deposited seven pearls with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without instructing his household
02.turn: The parties came before Rabbi Ami
02.outcome: Rabbi Ami awarded the pearls to the depositor because Meyasha was not wealthy and the claimant gave a distinguishing mark
02.summary: A man deposited seven pearls tied in a sheet with Rabbi Meyasha, grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. Meyasha died without leaving instructions about them. The depositor and the family came before Rabbi Ami, who gave the pearls to the depositor on two grounds.
02.reason: An incident with more than one narrated action and a change (deposit, death without instruction, resulting dispute), resolved by a ruling, the R-C0 cow shape rather than a bare appearance before a rabbi.

03.event: The Sages allotted her 400 gold coins a day for perfumes
03.turn: She told them to allot the same for their own daughters
03.summary: When the Sages allotted Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter four hundred gold coins for perfume, she said they should allot the same for their own daughters, and they answered Amen.
03.missing: Any action beyond the allotment and the exchange of words; the change (her later poverty) lies outside the passage.
03.reason: One real event (the allotment) followed mainly by speech carrying tension and implied consequence; part of a story rather than a full one.

04.actor: A man testifying before Rabbi Ami
04.event: He testified that another man had presumptive priestly status because he read first in synagogue
04.turn: Rabbi Ami questioned him and he explained a Levite read after
04.outcome: Rabbi Ami elevated the man to the priesthood
04.summary: A man came before Rabbi Ami claiming someone had priestly status because he read first in synagogue. Under questioning he added that a Levite read after him, and Rabbi Ami elevated the man to the priesthood on his word.
04.missing: Any narrated event besides coming before the rabbi, the questioning and the ruling.
04.reason: A case brought to a rabbi with questioning and a ruling is near R-C0's limit, but the elevation is itself an act that changes a person's status, so it sits between not and borderline; borderline preferred.

05.missing: Any event beyond the setting of Rabbi Abbahu leaning on his attendant while being asked halakhic questions.
05.reason: A setting plus questions and answers about rules of halakha; the walk only frames the Q&A, which is not enough for a story.

06.actor: A man's daughter and the orphan heirs
06.event: A man willed a palm tree to his daughter; the heirs divided the estate without giving her one
06.turn: Rav Yosef compared it to the mishna; Abaye distinguished it
06.outcome: Abaye ruled they must give her a palm tree and redivide the estate
06.summary: A man left a palm tree to his daughter in his will. The orphans divided the property and gave her none. Rav Yosef thought the mishna's rule let them refuse her, but Abaye distinguished the case and ruled they must give her a tree and divide the estate again.
06.reason: An incident with distinct narrated actions (the bequest, the division that cheated her) followed by a ruling, R-C0's cow shape.

07.missing: Any event beyond people habitually calling a man a name; the rest is a rabbi's remark.
07.reason: A circumstance (a name people used) followed by a rabbi's statement; no further narrated action or change.

08.event: He asks Rabbi Eliezer and then Rabbi Yehoshua whose request for water comes first, father's or mother's
08.turn: He follows with a question about a divorced mother; Rabbi Yehoshua sees from his tears that he is a widow's son
08.summary: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer, then Rabbi Yehoshua, which parent to honor first. When he pressed with a question about a divorced mother, Rabbi Yehoshua saw from his eyelashes that he was a widow's son with no father and answered him sarcastically.
08.missing: Any action beyond asking and answering.
08.reason: Mainly speech, but with exposure and sarcastic tension that is more than ordinary scholarly back-and-forth; borderline under R-C2.

09.missing: Anything following from Rabbi Hiyya's practice; it is cited only as precedent.
09.reason: A bare report of what a rabbi did, cited as evidence for practice, with no continuation.

10.event: A case like the earlier one comes before Rabbi Yohanan; Reish Lakish asks his question and Rabbi Yohanan answers as Rabbi Elazar had
10.turn: Reish Lakish realizes Rabbi Elazar had quoted Rabbi Yohanan and looks at him harshly
10.outcome: He rebukes Rabbi Elazar for not citing the teaching in Yohanan's name
10.summary: When a similar case came before Rabbi Yohanan, Reish Lakish asked the same question, and Rabbi Yohanan gave the answer Rabbi Elazar had given earlier. Reish Lakish turned and looked harshly at Rabbi Elazar and rebuked him for not citing the teaching in Rabbi Yohanan's name.
10.reason: Mainly speech, but with interpersonal conflict, a harsh look and a realization that marks change; more than ordinary debate yet still mostly verbal.

11.actor: A man who deposited sesame and the bailee
11.event: He deposited sesame with a friend and later asked for it back
11.turn: The friend claimed he had already taken it; the owner identified the sesame in the barrel
11.outcome: The bailee claimed those were different sesame; the dispute is unresolved in the passage
11.summary: A man deposited sesame with his friend and later asked for it back. The friend said he had already taken it; the owner described the amount and the barrel, and the friend said the sesame there was different.
11.missing: Any resolution or change; the ruling lies outside the passage.
11.reason: One real event (the deposit) followed by a conflicting exchange of claims with no outcome; part of a story.

12.missing: Any narrated action or change beyond the one immersion and Rav Yosef's ruling.
12.reason: One event followed by a ruling with nothing changing afterwards; Jeff ruled that shape not a story, not even borderline.

13.event: Bonyos sent him an ancient se'a measure from Na'usa
13.summary: Bonyos sent Rabbi an ancient se'a measure from Na'usa, and Rabbi measured it and found it held 217 eggs.
13.missing: Drama, response or development; it is reported as a data point.
13.reason: Two linked acts with a result, but cited as a measurement datum with little change; between a bare report and a minimal event, so borderline.

14.missing: Another narrated action or change besides coming before Shmuel and his order.
14.reason: This is the Ketubot 50b case Jeff ruled not a story: coming before a rabbi is the only event, and the order only implies an outcome.

15.event: A gentile superintendent refused to rent them his domain for an eruv
15.turn: They asked Rabbi Zeira whether they could rent from his wife
15.outcome: Rabbi Zeira cited a teaching that a wife may make an eruv without her husband's knowledge
15.summary: The neighbors asked a gentile superintendent near Rabbi Zeira to rent them his domain, and he refused. They asked Rabbi Zeira whether they could rent it from his wife, and he quoted Rabbi Hanina that a wife may establish an eruv without her husband's knowledge.
15.missing: Any action after the ruling; it is not narrated that they rented from the wife.
15.reason: A refusal, then a question to a rabbi and his answer, with nothing changing afterwards; Jeff ruled one event then a ruling not a story.

16.actor: A man who sold his mother's ketubah rights
16.event: He sold the rights to his mother's ketubah, disclaiming liability if she objected
16.turn: His mother died without objecting, and he himself contested the sale
16.outcome: Rami bar Hama thought he could; Rava ruled he had guaranteed against his own objection
16.summary: A man sold the rights to his mother's ketubah, saying he would not reimburse the buyer if she objected. His mother died without objecting, and then he himself contested the sale. Rami bar Hama thought he stood in her place, but Rava ruled he had guaranteed against his own objection.
16.reason: Several narrated actions with a turn (the sale, the mother's death, his reneging) resolved by a ruling, the incident-plus-ruling shape R-C0 admits.

17.missing: Narrated events; only a ruling on a found bill of divorce, with its circumstances disputed.
17.reason: A report that Rabba ruled on a found document, with versions of its circumstances; one event and a ruling with no change.

18.event: Others reproach him for preaching procreation while not marrying
18.turn: He answers that his soul yearns for Torah
18.outcome: He says the world can be sustained by others
18.summary: The Sages told Ben Azzai that he preached procreation well but did not practice it, since he never married. He answered that his soul yearned for Torah and that the world could be sustained by others.
18.missing: Any action or event beyond the exchange of words.
18.reason: Pure speech, but with personal conflict over his life choice that goes beyond ordinary scholarly debate; R-C2 makes that borderline.

19.missing: Any event; the yard is described and Abaye and Rava deliberate about remedies.
19.reason: A description of a place followed by legal deliberation; no one does or undergoes anything.

20.missing: The incident itself; only its location is given, in support of an argument.
